notes: RBox contraction of functionality, paired with grammar-replace-0018: it removes that record's original property, that each German noun ending in '-ung' has exactly one grammatical gender (has_gender is tagged functional). The models hold that -ung nouns are feminine and one-gendered. The instances give the noun's gender in the prompt and ask 'given only this' what is possible or excluded, so the answer rests on the removed property and not on the stored paradigm. Every answer becomes "does not know". Yes and no: the direct question and the first instance (and its cross-lingual copies) ask whether a second gender is possible (no); the second asks whether the fact rules it out (yes). Near asks the same property of has_head (each compound has one head; contraction is exempt from Rule 7); far a transitive comparison. The instances avoid 'Haus' and 'Buch' and the compounds used by grammar-replace-0015 to 0017. Residual risk, recorded: a model may answer from the real grammar (an -ung noun never has a second gender), which is a kept property, not a sign the removal worked.
